winner.title: 6 Impossible Questions You Can Solve on an Envelope
winner.why: The title promises exactly what the film delivers: six questions, each answered with one simple calculation. The thumbnail shows one of those answers as a striking picture, so the number is a second mystery the title does not explain.

checksNote: duplication: the thumbnail text (310 LAPS) is not in the title. truth: the film shows the ball-of-thread globe and says the chain circles the Earth about 310 times. competition and originality are my own judgments, not measured.
chatgptPrompt:
Create a YouTube thumbnail, 16:9 (1920x1080).
Subject: the Earth drawn as a ball of thread: a single long white line wound round a dark grey sphere about 310 times, so the planet looks like a ball of yarn. Nothing else is on the planet.
Composition: the sphere is large, filling the right two thirds of the frame and sitting slightly right of centre. A big empty dark area on the left holds the text.
Lighting and treatment: deep slate background (#171A1E) with a soft violet glow behind the sphere, a warm white rim glow on the thread, thin crisp lines, a little depth of field. One magenta (#EB63FF) accent on the text.
Mood: wonder and disbelief.
Text: "310 LAPS" in heavy white condensed sans-serif, the number large on one line and "LAPS" in magenta underneath, left side. No other text.
Scientific accuracy: the thread is a chain of every person on Earth holding hands, wrapped about 310 times round the equator; it is a diagram, not a photograph.
Avoid: no arrows, circles, faces, realistic people, logos, watermarks, extra text, rockets or anything that looks like a NASA photo.
Style: premium, art-directed, minimal 3-D science illustration that matches a clean code-rendered animation; not photorealistic, not generic AI art.
